name: Peizhu (Pam) Qian
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science; Presidential Frontier Faculty
fitReason: Strong computational HRI fit through human behavior and collaborative-task models, explainable robot policies and vision-based physical skill feedback. Her new Houston group combines AI methods with healthcare and workforce training; concrete robotic tutoring predates her faculty move.

physicalEvidence.summary: First-authored RSS 2025 ASTRID, completed at Rice, uses an actual Stretch mobile manipulator, off-board depth camera and computer. MediaPipe learned pose estimation feeds geometric compliance checks and real-time audiovisual feedback. The robot performs preprogrammed movements and scripted interruptions, rather than learned manipulation. A nine-participant feasibility study used a simulated patient in a physical training room. PS-PRM is additional Rice collaborative Stretch 2/UR5 evidence, not proof that those platforms are now installed in her Houston group. August 2026 WILLIE is a wound-image transformer benchmark, not robot deployment.

shortVisit.summary: The live join page welcomes undergraduate and MS research inquiries with CV, interests and transcript, but requires at least one semester and 10 hours/week. Only the undergraduate REU paragraph expressly includes students from outside UH. External-master’s eligibility and an eight-week summer exception remain unverified. The page was last updated November 21, 2025; its Fall 2026 PhD and 12-month postdoc notices are not summer 2027 short-visit opportunities.

scoreReasons.fit: 39/40: direct computational HRI, explainable policies and embodied skill tutoring.
scoreReasons.physical: 20/25: clear personally attributable first-author physical system, but at prior Rice institution; current Houston inventory unverified.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: 0/20: explicit MS inquiry has semester minimum and no verified external-master’s short-visit eligibility.
scoreReasons.freshness: 15/15: substantive August 2026 Houston-group vision-transformer release; principal physical tutoring experiment remains 2025 and is marked accordingly.

unknowns: The stated minimum is one semester; do not silently equate this with an eight-week visit. Whether a summer term counts requires confirmation.
Physical evidence is prior-Rice or collaborative; current Houston hardware inventory and a completed Houston robotic deployment were not verified.
A separate current Houston supplement describes possible central visitor categories, but personal-only funding, appointment classification and host approval remain unresolved.

A healthcare-related project must be scoped within the approved category; UH Student Intern rules exclude patient-care/contact work. Bench, simulation or training research access is not automatically granted.
WILLIE is research-only wound-image analysis; its author model card explicitly disclaims clinical use and does not establish a physical robot result.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
